title: Деньги в урне и звонок Шефу  (Money in the Trash Bin and Calling the Chef)

segments.t: On the second ransom call, Rodion scolds Nastya's father for bringing Kostya along and instructs him to drop the money into a trash bin around the corner. Back at the restaurant, Max calls Chef Barinov in desperation to tell him the dining room is overflowing.

Now let's go back through the conversation line by line.

'You should not have brought Konstantin along with you.' Rodion continues plainly without holding back, letting the remark speak for itself.
'Yes, hello.' Barinov voices this warning beside Rodion: spoken Russian trims this down to just 2 words, dropping the extra helper words that English has to spell out.
'We know everything that happened.' Rodion brings that remark calmly now: spoken Russian trims this down to just 4 words, dropping the extra helper words that English has to spell out.
'How did you find out?' Barinov quizzes promptly about what Rodion just brought up.
'There is a shop on the other side of the street.' Rodion centers one memorable choice toward Barinov: "magazin" means "shop", and it carries the main weight of what Rodion is saying.

'Right there, around the corner to the right, is a trash bin.' Barinov lays out the remark without pause: notice how Russian needs no word for "am", "is", or "are" in the present — placing the words side by side says it all.
'Put the money inside it and walk away.' Rodion responds firmly hearing Barinov, shifting the whole mood of the room in a single beat.

'Rodion Sergeyevich?' Barinov hands over that reply with candor: Russian keeps the exact word order of a normal statement here, turning it into a question for Rodion purely through rising pitch at the end.

'Otherwise I am going to be late for work already.' Rodion answers quietly toward Barinov, keeping the focus on what actually matters here.
'All by myself? Well?' Barinov tests earnestly as Rodion tries to explain the situation.
'Only for your sake.' Rodion focuses on one telling word on cue: "tolko" means "only", and it carries the main weight of what Rodion is saying.
'At the Claude Monet restaurant.' Barinov shares this update frankly here: spoken Russian trims this down to just 4 words, dropping the extra helper words that English has to spell out.
'Because the thing is.' Rodion chimes in pointedly with a sigh, letting the remark speak for itself.
